one_month_reasoning: The window to 2026-11-08 very likely contains Paycom's Q3 2026 report: last year the date notice came Oct 15 and results Nov 5 (after close), and the Q3 10-Q filing also starts the clock on Richison's 10b5-1 sales, which cannot begin before Dec 1, so no founder selling falls inside the window. Q3 guidance was not given. The raised FY26 guide (midpoint $2.2045B less H1 $1,103.1M) implies H2 revenue of about $1,101M, only +6.1% y/y against Q2's +9.8%, so the bar looks low and a beat-and-raise is the modal outcome. Against that, estimates were raised after the August beat and the stock already trades near its $244.98 high, so a beat may be priced in, and float income and bookings commentary can swing the reaction either way. PAYC's earnings-day moves are large (the Q2 print re-rated the stock), so I use a slightly wider than normal 1-month sigma of ~13.5% (vs. 46%/3.5 = 13.1%) with a near-neutral median of ~$233.5. Short-horizon calls that are wrong are penalised, so I lean on symmetry.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (65%: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~$15.0 x 17x peer-median multiple = $255) and a 5-year DCF (35%: FCF after SBC from $679M in 2028, 7-8% growth, 9.0% WACC, 3% terminal, net debt $785M less $633M retained FCF, 45.07M shares = $285). The blend is about $266.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS (Oct-2027) $15.0 = 0.25 x FY27 consensus $13.97 + 0.75 x FY28E $15.37; x 17.0x (peer median 17.19x).

inputs_detail.derivation: $13.97 x 1.10. +10% = recurring revenue growth ~8% (2026 guide 8-9%, FY27 consensus revenue +7.44%) + ~1pt margin leverage (adj. EBITDA margin guided to 46% from 43% in 2025) + ~3% net share-count reduction (FCF >$650M less ~$68M dividends funds ~$550M/yr of buybacks, ~5% of the $10.5B market cap at today's price) - ~2pts from higher revolver interest ($900M drawn; Q2 interest expense $10.5M, ~$42M annualized).

Peer median forward P/E 17.19x (11 peers, range 7.6x-23.0x); PAYC trades at 17.68x today. 17x = at/just under the median: higher margins (46% adj. EBITDA) and buyback-boosted EPS growth offset by slower revenue growth than PCTY/WDAY/TYL, new revolver leverage, founder 10b5-1 selling and the AI-disruption discount applied to seat-based HCM. No premium is claimed.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Valued at Oct-2027. FCF less SBC: 2028 $679M, 2029 $726M, 2030 $776M, 2031 $829M, 2032 $886M; WACC 9.0%; terminal growth 3%. PV of explicit FCF $3.13B + PV of terminal value $9.85B = EV $12.98B, less $785M net debt plus $633M retained FCF = $12.83B equity / 45.07M shares = $285. At a 9.5% WACC the value is $263.

inputs_detail.derivation: $650M x ~1.08: revenue growth ~7.4-8% (consensus/guide), capex held ~6% of revenue (CFO, Q2 call).
2028 = $700M x 1.08; then growth fades to 7% (recurring revenue +10.3% in 2025, guided +8-9% in 2026).
CFO: SBC ~3% of revenue in 2026; treated as a cash-equivalent cost (revenue grown 8%/yr from $2.2045B guide midpoint).

Cost of equity = 5.22% (10y UST) + 1.0 x 4.20% (implied ERP) = 9.42%; beta 1.0 chosen above reported 5Y beta 0.83 given 46% realized vol. Debt $900M at Term SOFR + 1.25-2.00% (~5.9% pre-tax, 4.3% after 27% non-GAAP tax). Weights $10.47B equity / $0.9B debt -> 9.0%.
Roughly nominal GDP; below 5.22% risk-free and well below 2025 recurring growth of 10.3%.
$982.8M total debt ($900M revolver + leases) less $198.0M cash at 2026-06-30.
~$700M FCF less ~$68M dividends ($0.375/qtr x 45M shares); used for debt paydown or buybacks at ~fair value, so added to equity.

bear.story: The AI-disruption narrative for seat-based HCM returns, or Q4/2027 guidance shows recurring growth slipping to ~5-6% as the new-rep cohort under-delivers. The margin gains of 2026 (R&D cut, labour efficiencies) prove one-off. Founder 10b5-1 selling of up to 1.09M shares (Dec 2026 to Jun 2027) and $900M of revolver debt weigh on the multiple. Result: ~12x on ~$13 EPS, taking the stock back toward where management was buying ($127-135 average in H1 2026).

base.story: Recurring growth runs 8-9% and adj. EBITDA margin holds ~46%. Buybacks continue at a slower pace now that the price is higher, EPS compounds ~10-12%, and the stock holds roughly today's ~16-17x forward multiple on a rolled-forward NTM EPS of ~$15. A street that is still Hold-rated (avg PT $220) and the founder selling cap the re-rating, so the price ends a little under the $266 fundamental value.

bull.story: The ~100 extra sales reps and in-app purchases (Asset Management, Career & Succession, IWant-driven upsell) re-accelerate recurring growth to 10%+. Self-hosted AI keeps compounding savings (management cites ~$100M of R&D and ~$30M of third-party AI fees saved in 2026), margins push toward 48%, and 2027 FCF clears $750M. The stock earns ~20x on ~$16 NTM EPS.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 7.6x (ASUR) to 23.0x (TYL), median 17.19x. Estimated forward EV/EBITDA 9.0x (ASUR) to 61.5x (NSP, depressed EBITDA), median ~14.1x. 5 of the 11 peers are named PAYC competitors (ADP, PAYX, PCTY, WDAY, INTU). Dayforce (taken private) and Oracle/SAP/ServiceNow/UKG (too diversified or private) are excluded. TNET, NSP and ASUR add SMB HR/payroll exposure, and TYL, BR and JKHY add mature recurring-software profiles because there are not 10 listed pure-play HCM names.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17.0x forward P/E: at or just below the 17.19x peer median and below PAYC's own current 17.68x (StockAnalysis). PAYC screens cheap on EV/EBITDA (~10.9x 2026 adj. EBITDA midpoint $1.0145B on $11.07B EV, vs. a ~14x peer median), but I do not use that multiple. PAYC's adjusted EBITDA excludes SBC (~3% of revenue) and is followed by heavy own-data-centre capex (~6% of revenue, $271M in 2025), so EBITDA-to-FCF conversion is lower than at asset-light peers.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium or discount: the multiple sits inside the peer range at the median. PAYC's structural positives (highest adj. EBITDA margin in the group at ~46%, revenue retention up to 91%, net cash generation >$650M) are offset by revenue growth (7-8% total) that is no higher than PCTY's or INTU's, new leverage ($900M revolver), concentrated founder control and selling (13.1% holder, 10b5-1 plan), and weak shareholder support on pay (say-on-pay ~61% for at the 2026 meeting). I cannot show that these net out to a durable premium, so I use the median.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$150 (-35%) the stock would have given back the whole post-Q2 re-rating and would be trading near the $127-135 average prices of the H1 2026 buybacks. That would most likely mean the 2027 guide (Feb 2027) or a quarterly print showed recurring growth falling toward ~5% or revenue retention slipping from 91%, i.e. AI or price competition is actually eroding seats or modules, or that the 2026 margin step-up reversed. Ordinary volatility (46% realized) seldom moves a stock this far with fundamentals intact.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results and FY26 guide update (implied H2 growth only ~6% leaves room to beat)
Ernest Group/Richison 10b5-1 plan may sell up to 1.09M shares (~2.4% of shares out)
Q4 2026 results, first 2027 guidance, annual revenue retention and headcount disclosure
Buybacks under the $2B plan ($1.66B remaining at Q2 end)
Fed rate path: ~$105M of 2026 revenue is interest on ~$2.9-3.1B of client funds; cuts reduce it
Q1 2027 results (forms-filing seasonal high) and annual meeting (2026 say-on-pay only ~61% for)
Q2 2027 results: test of whether new products and the expanded sales force lift bookings

key_uncertainties: Whether generative AI and agentic HR tools erode per-employee/module pricing or lower switching costs for SMB and mid-market HCM (the 'AI prophecy' behind the 52-week low of $104.90).
Sustainability of the 2026 margin step-up (R&D down sharply in Q2; 46% adj. EBITDA guide vs 44% initially) and whether it starves growth investment.
Bookings: ~100 new reps and teams of 8 expanded to 10; management says bookings are only 'as expected', with no hard inflection yet.
Capital allocation now that the stock has re-rated: buyback pace, revolver paydown, and capex if the data-centre build resumes (Q1 call: 'not ready to give guidance').
Interest-rate path for float income (~5% of revenue) and for revolver cost.
Founder supply (10b5-1) and governance (a weak say-on-pay vote; ex-insiders added to the board).
reasoning: Primary-document read: Q2 2026 (8-K, 10-Q, call) showed revenue +9.8%, recurring +11%, adj. EBITDA margin 44.2% (+320bp), FY26 guide raised to $2.197-2.212B and adj. EBITDA $1.007-1.022B (~46%), and FCF guided to >$650M. The less-covered filings show a balance-sheet transformation. Paycom bought back 10.9M shares (~20%) in H1 2026 for ~$1.4B (Q1 average $126.61) and funded it with a new $2.125B secured revolver ($900M drawn; leverage covenant 3.5x; maturity 2031). Shares outstanding fell from 54.3M (Feb) to 45.07M (Jul 28), and a new $2B no-expiry authorization was approved May 4 ($1.66B left). That share shrink, not just operations, drives the FY27 consensus EPS of $13.97 (+15%). Off-consensus negatives from filings: Richison/Ernest Group adopted a 10b5-1 plan on Sept 1 to sell up to 1.09M shares from Dec 1, 2026; the President sold at $237-240 in late August; the 2026 say-on-pay passed with only ~61% support; Q2 R&D fell sharply, which the CEO attributes to self-hosted AI models (~$100M R&D savings). Valuation: P/E at the 17.19x peer median on Oct-2027 NTM EPS of ~$15 gives $255. The DCF (9.0% WACC from a 5.22% 10y and 4.20% ERP, 3% terminal) gives $285 (and $263 at 9.5%). The 65/35 blend is $266, ~15% above $232.22. The sell-side is more cautious (Hold, avg PT $220, range $160-286). Distribution: a scenario mixture of bear $155/25%, base $245/50%, bull $315/25%, each lognormal with 18-25% sigma, gives a median of ~$241, a mean of ~$245 and a log-sd of ~0.33. That is wider than a typical large cap (25-35%) but below the 46% realized vol, which was inflated by the slump to $104.90 and the rebound since, so I fatten the tails slightly. P(>=232) = 0.55, i.e. a modest positive drift from earnings growth plus buybacks, held back by founder supply and the AI-multiple risk. Research was limited where transcripts were image PDFs or paywalled (the GuruFocus and Insider Monkey Q4 transcripts were not bypassed). The Q2 call text came from a transcript data feed and was cross-checked against TipRanks for the FCF, capex and authorization figures. No option prices or implied volatility were used.
